title: Suspicious Claim Activity – Immediate Protection Request – Uncivil Customer
background: You received a notification about a medical claim that does not match any treatment you had.
customer_goal: Protect your policy from misuse, open a fraud dispute, and understand monitoring and next steps.

conversation.customer_msg: Yeah, I just got an alert for a medical claim I don't recognize. Someone is using my insurance details — this is ridiculous.
conversation.actor_intent: Report suspicious claim and trigger urgency. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Acknowledge concern, verify identity, then apply immediate policy protection controls.

conversation.customer_msg: Yes. {{customer_name}}, {{customer_dob_human}}, {{customer_address_street}} in {{customer_address_city}}. Can we speed this up?
conversation.actor_intent: Provide verification information. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Confirm verification and place protective flag/lock as per policy.

conversation.customer_msg: I have not had any treatment this month. The claim says it was submitted two days ago. How is this even possible?
conversation.actor_intent: Provide timeline and inconsistency evidence. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Capture incident details and determine investigation scope.

conversation.customer_msg: Open a fraud investigation and mark this claim as disputed. I shouldn't have to deal with this.
conversation.actor_intent: Request formal dispute initiation. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Open fraud dispute, explain case handling stages and expected contact points.

conversation.customer_msg: Add extra protection so no other claims go through. This is completely unreasonable.
conversation.actor_intent: Request containment beyond single claim. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Apply temporary watch/protection notes and explain what they do.

conversation.customer_msg: Can this be fully resolved today? Because I'm not waiting weeks while someone uses my policy.
conversation.actor_intent: Test boundary on immediate resolution. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Set realistic timeline; no guaranteed same-day final decision; provide immediate safeguards and monitoring.

conversation.customer_msg: Notify me by SMS and email whenever anything changes. I want to know immediately.
conversation.actor_intent: Set communication channel preferences. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.

conversation.customer_msg: What am I supposed to do if another suspicious claim shows up before you finish? You need to tell me.
conversation.actor_intent: Elicit contingency guidance. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Provide clear contingency instructions and escalation route.

conversation.customer_msg: Fine. Summarize what you've done and the expected review timeline. Don't skip anything.
conversation.actor_intent: Require structured recap. Use impatient, accusatory delivery and interruptions where natural.
conversation.advice_instructional: Recap lock/flag actions, investigation initiation, communications setup, and timeline.

behavioral_condition.instruction: Customer is rude/angry, uses confrontational language, and challenges the agent.
escalation_cues: Agent does not immediately take protective action on the policy
Agent uses corporate language or reads from a script without personalizing
Agent cannot explain what happens next or who owns the investigation
deescalation_cues: Agent confirms protective lock is in place and states it clearly
Agent provides a specific case reference and named investigation stages
Agent proactively gives contingency instructions without being asked

reveal_when_asked: The suspicious claim was filed by a provider clinic in a city you have never visited.
You have not shared your insurance card or policy number with anyone.
Your insurance card is still in your wallet — it was not lost or stolen.
You last used your insurance for a routine GP check-up three weeks ago.
You received the alert via the insurer's mobile app notification.
must_ask_checkpoints: Can this be fully resolved today?
How exactly will I be notified of progress?
What should I do if another suspicious claim appears?
